newsitem.title: THAILAND: No change to exchange rate - Bank of Thailand.
newsitem.headline: No change to exchange rate - Bank of Thailand.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Tuesday reaffirmed it had no plans to change the exchange rate mechanism.
"There remain rumours in the market about possible changes in Thailand's exchange rate mechanism," the central bank said in a statement.
"The Bank of Thailand reaffirms our denial issued last Friday that there will be no change in the exchange rate mechanism."
Rumours circulated in stock and money markets late last week that Thai authorities might be planning a change to the exchange rate mechanism that could lead to a widening of the band.
The baht is fixed against three major currencies in a trade-weighed basket dominated by the U.S. dollar.
The Bank of Thailand fixes a dollar/baht mid-rate on a daily basis. It buys the dollar two satangs below and sells two satangs above the mid-rate through commercial banks.
Officials from the central bank denied the rumours and Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh on Sunday reaffirmed the government had no plans to devalue the baht.
But some traders said there were still lingering effects of the talk in the market early this week.

The financial markets have been hit by worries over the sluggish Thai economy and questions over the feasibility of various Thai government efforts to bolster growth and help cash-strapped property and finance sectors.
The Thai bourse has been spiralling downward and has plunged to more than six year lows.
